entities.name: PMID:25441651
observations: Australian LSAC kindergarten cohort (n=4,983; SHCN subsample n=720) identified high, average, and low academic trajectories from ages 4–5 to 10–11 years.
Established or emerging SHCN increased likelihood of weaker academic trajectories; emerging SHCN had adjusted relative risk 3.06 (95% CI 1.03–9.10).
Evidence included less-complex SHCN but did not report separate mild, moderate, and severe estimates.

entities.name: PMID:26724181
observations: In 576 preterm/low-birth-weight children, Woodcock–Johnson math and reading were measured at ages 8 and 18.
SHCN defined by medication or medical-service use, special therapies, or functional limitation was associated with lower achievement; math declined from 97.5 to 90.1 and reading from 99.0 to 96.8.
The analysis compared SHCN versus non-SHCN rather than explicit severity strata.

entities.name: PMID:37554667
observations: Norwegian registry study of 247,120 students aged 15–16 years found severe disabilities generally had more negative GPA associations than less-severe disabilities.
Effects were condition-specific: strongest for ADHD and autism and notable for epilepsy, while asthma and diabetes had GPA comparable to peers.
GPA was measured at one educational stage, not as a repeated childhood trajectory.

entities.name: PMID:39631793
observations: German prospective cohort (n=751) assessed SHCN before school entry, at end of first grade, and end of third grade.
Ever-SHCN, current SHCN, emerging SHCN, and persistent SHCN were associated with poorer third-grade German/math/science grades; adjusted mean differences ranged from 0.17 to 0.31 grades.
The study assessed timing and persistence rather than formal mild–moderate–severe strata.

entities.name: PMID:37352302
observations: German prospective cohort (n=1,921) found SHCN associated with increased illness-related absence (adjusted rate ratio 1.37, 95% CI 1.16–1.62).
Functional limitations, emotional/behavioral/developmental treatment, and at least two SHCN consequences showed the strongest associations.
This supports a burden/number-of-needs gradient relevant to school functioning but did not directly repeat academic achievement.

entities.name: PMID:35909577
observations: Welsh linkage study of 150 children with cystic fibrosis found lower-than-population attainment at age 10–11 years: 77% English, 81% mathematics, and 82% science expected attainment.
Hospital admissions as a severity marker did not significantly distinguish attainment within the cystic fibrosis group.
This indicates condition-specific heterogeneity and weak support for a simple severity gradient in cystic fibrosis.

entities.name: Learning-severity evidence
observations: Across CSHCN studies, greater health burden, functional limitation, persistence, or disability severity is generally associated with poorer learning or school functioning.

Evidence for explicit graded severity is strongest in cross-sectional registry GPA data; longitudinal studies more often compare SHCN status, persistence, emergence, or burden than formal severity levels.
Condition-specific heterogeneity means severity does not predict learning uniformly across all diagnoses.

entities.name: Pregnancy-associated renal colic
observations: Acute flank pain radiating to the groin with marked hematuria and no pyuria or nitrites is clinically consistent with suspected ureteral stone during pregnancy.
Renal and bladder ultrasound with Doppler is the recommended initial imaging study in pregnancy.
Noncontrast MR urography is preferred second-line imaging when ultrasound is nondiagnostic or equivocal.
Ionizing-radiation studies, including CT, are reserved for unresolved cases when clinically essential.

entities.name: Renal ultrasound
observations: Kidney-and-bladder ultrasound, ideally with Doppler, is the most appropriate next test for suspected nephrolithiasis in a pregnant patient.

entities.name: MR urography
observations: Noncontrast MR urography is a preferred second-line study after nondiagnostic or equivocal ultrasound in pregnancy.
